\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অনুমান} \bn{করা} (ônumān kôrā)}{অনুমান করা (ônumān kôrā)}]{\bn{অনুমান} \bn{করা} (ônumān kôrā) — to suppose; to infer}

\label{lesson:BN-C367-onuman-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for rare, then the Bengali for to assume.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অনুমান} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{অনুমান} \bn{করা}} — \emph{ônumān kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to suppose; to infer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমি} \bn{অনুমান} \bn{করলাম} \bn{যে} \bn{বাস} \bn{দেরি} \bn{করলে} \bn{অরুণ} \bn{ট্যাক্সি} \bn{নেবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmi ônumān kôrlām je bās deri kôrle ôrun ṭæksi nebe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I guessed that if the bus was late, Arun would take a taxi.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ঠিক} \bn{অনুমান} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini ṭhik ônumān kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অনুমান} \bn{করা}} (\emph{ônumān kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{anumāna}, inference (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}: to reason from what you see to what you cannot.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ônumān kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ônumān kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmi ônumān kôrlām je bās deri kôrle ôrun ṭæksi nebe.} — I guessed that if the bus was late, Arun would take a taxi.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for rare, then the Bengali for to assume, then say \emph{ônumān kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অনুমান} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To suppose; to infer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করা} (āndāj kôrā)}{আন্দাজ করা (āndāj kôrā)}]{\bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করা} (āndāj kôrā) — to estimate; to make a rough guess}

\label{lesson:BN-C367-andaj-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to assume, then the Bengali for to suppose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{āndāj kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to estimate; to make a rough guess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করো}, \bn{ট্যাক্সিতে} \bn{গেলে} \bn{কত} \bn{খরচ} \bn{হবে}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āndāj kôro, ṭæksite gele kôtô khôrôch hôbe?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Have a guess: how much will it cost if we go by taxi?
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{দামটা} \bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini dāmṭā āndāj kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{āndāj kôrā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{andāz}, a measure or estimate, with \bn{করা}: to judge an amount by eye.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āndāj kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āndāj kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āndāj kôro, ṭæksite gele kôtô khôrôch hôbe?} — Have a guess: how much will it cost if we go by taxi?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to assume, then the Bengali for to suppose, then say \emph{āndāj kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আন্দাজ} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To estimate; to make a rough guess\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আভাস} (ābhās)}{আভাস (ābhās)}]{\bn{আভাস} (ābhās) — a hint; an indication}

\label{lesson:BN-C367-abhas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to suppose, then the Bengali for to estimate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আভাস}}
\textbf{\bn{আভাস}} — \emph{ābhās} — \textquotedblleft{}a hint; an indication\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আকাশ} \bn{কালো} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{ঝড়ের} \bn{আভাস} \bn{পাই।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ākāsh kālo hôle āmrā jhôṛer ābhās pāi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the sky turns dark, we get a hint of a storm.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আভাস}} (\emph{ābhās}) is Sanskrit \emph{ābhāsa}, appearance (Monier-Williams). Bengali uses it for the faint appearance of something still to come, a hint.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ābhās}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ābhās}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ākāsh kālo hôle āmrā jhôṛer ābhās pāi.} — When the sky turns dark, we get a hint of a storm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to suppose, then the Bengali for to estimate, then say \emph{ābhās} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আভাস} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hint; an indication\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রত্যাশা} (prôtyāshā)}{প্রত্যাশা (prôtyāshā)}]{\bn{প্রত্যাশা} (prôtyāshā) — an expectation}

\label{lesson:BN-C367-protyasha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to estimate, then the Bengali for a hint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রত্যাশা}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রত্যাশা}} — \emph{prôtyāshā} — \textquotedblleft{}an expectation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ফলাফল} \bn{যদি} \bn{প্রত্যাশার} \bn{চেয়ে} \bn{ভালো} \bn{হয়}, \bn{তাহলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{পার্টি} \bn{দেব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{phôlāphôl jôdi prôtyāshār cheye bhālo hôy, tāhôle āmrā pārṭi debô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the results are better than expected, we'll throw a party.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রত্যাশা}} (\emph{prôtyāshā}) is Sanskrit \emph{pratyāśā}, hope or expectation (Monier-Williams), with \emph{āśā}, hope, at its heart.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôtyāshā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôtyāshā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phôlāphôl jôdi prôtyāshār cheye bhālo hôy, tāhôle āmrā pārṭi debô.} — If the results are better than expected, we'll throw a party.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to estimate, then the Bengali for a hint, then say \emph{prôtyāshā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{প্রত্যাশা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An expectation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভবিষ্যৎ} (bhôbishyôt)}{ভবিষ্যৎ (bhôbishyôt)}]{\bn{ভবিষ্যৎ} (bhôbishyôt) — the future}

\label{lesson:BN-C367-bhobishyot}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a hint, then the Bengali for an expectation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভবিষ্যৎ}}
\textbf{\bn{ভবিষ্যৎ}} — \emph{bhôbishyôt} — \textquotedblleft{}the future\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এখন} \bn{টাকা} \bn{জমালে} \bn{ভবিষ্যৎ} \bn{নিরাপদ} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ekhôn ṭākā jômāle bhôbishyôt nirāpôd hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you save money now, your future will be secure.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভবিষ্যৎ}} (\emph{bhôbishyôt}) is Sanskrit \emph{bhaviṣyat}, 'what is going to be' (Monier-Williams). The last letter is \bn{ৎ}, a t with no vowel after it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhôbishyôt}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhôbishyôt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekhôn ṭākā jômāle bhôbishyôt nirāpôd hôbe.} — If you save money now, your future will be secure.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a hint, then the Bengali for an expectation, then say \emph{bhôbishyôt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ভবিষ্যৎ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The future\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
